title: Mobile Video: How to check and configure firewall exceptions for VideoManager EX (VMEX)
summary: Verify and configure Windows Defender Firewall inbound rules so DC-200, M500, M500E, SVX, V700, Transfer Station II, and browsers can reach VideoManager EX on ports 9080–9082 (plus optional ONStream ports 554 and 8101).
body:
Article metadata. Created on: 2026-04-29 14:38:16. Updated on: 2026-04-30 18:58:37. Views: 87. Product Categories — Tier 1: Mobile Video; Tier 2: Mobile Video Software; Tier 3: Video Manager EX (Cloud). Visible to: Guest, Customer, Internal, Partner.

Topic/Objective
The objective of this article is to resolve connectivity issues where DC-200, M500, V700, or Transfer Station II devices fail to connect to VideoManager EX (VMEX). Common symptoms include:
- Devices displaying statuses such as "Configured/Disconnected" or "Open/Connected" (prior to full configuration).
- Networked computers are unable to access the VMEX interface, even though the service is operational on the host server.

Scope/Context
This guide applies to on-premises installations of VideoManager EX where local network or server firewalls may be blocking the necessary communication ports. It is intended for system administrators or IT personnel responsible for managing the server environment.

Background/Details
For VideoManager EX to communicate with body-worn cameras, in-car video systems, and client browsers, specific ports must be open to allow inbound traffic. If these ports are restricted by the Windows Defender Firewall, devices will appear offline or unreachable.

Outcome/Recommendation
Follow these steps to verify and configure the necessary firewall exceptions.

1. Verify Existing Rules
1. Open Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security.
2. Navigate to Inbound Rules in the left-hand pane.
3. Check for the rules listed in the table below. Ensure they are enabled (indicated by a green checkmark).

2. Required Ports and Protocols
If the following rules do not exist, they must be created manually (either as combined TCP/UDP rules or individual rules):

Service: User interface and API | Default Port: 9080 | Protocol: TCP | Details: Required to access the VideoManager frontend in the browser or to use the REST API. | Enabled by default on installation: Yes
Service: VideoManager sites | Default Port: 9080 | Protocol: TCP | Details: Required to allow VideoManager sites to connect to Central VideoManager and vice-versa. | Enabled by default: Yes
Service: Access control key authenticated devices | Default Port: 9081 | Protocol: TCP | Details: Required for devices to connect to VideoManager (VT50, VT100, V200, VB400, V500). | Enabled by default: Yes
Service: Client certificate authenticated devices | Default Port: 9082 | Protocol: TCP | Details: Required for devices to connect to VideoManager (M500/M500E/SVX/V700). | Enabled by default: Yes
Service: ONStream / RTSP streaming | Default Port: 554 | Protocol: TCP / UDP | Details: Optional — only required if ONStream is enabled for RTSP streaming to other services. | Enabled by default: No
Service: ONStream / ONVIF | Default Port: 8101 | Protocol: TCP | Details: Optional — only required if ONStream is enabled and ONVIF connection is needed. | Enabled by default: No
Service: Client certificate authenticated users | Default Port: [not set] | Protocol: TCP | Details: Optional — only required if using Client Certificate Authentication to log into VideoManager. Not set up by default. Port must be set in Admin > Web server when adding. | Enabled by default: No

3. Create New Firewall Rules
If any ports are missing, create a new rule:
1. From the Actions menu on the right, click New Rule.
2. Select Port and click Next.
3. Select TCP or UDP and enter the specific local ports from the table above.
4. Select "Allow the connection" (Note: Use "Allow the connection if it is secure" only if your environment specifically requires IPsec).
5. Apply the rule to the Domain, Private, and Public profiles as appropriate for your network.
6. Name the rule clearly (e.g., "VideoManager EX - Device Connectivity").

4. Finalize Configuration
1. Restart the PSS Manager: Ensure VMEX is not currently in use by other operators before restarting the service.
2. Verify Connectivity: Check the Dock Manager or VideoManager interface to confirm that docks and devices now show as Connected.
